type O = { f(n: number): number; c: number; arr: number[]; g(): O };

const o: O = {
  f: (n) => n * 10,
  c: 2,
  arr: [5, 6, 7],
  g: () => o,
};

function narrowedArgument(a: O | undefined) {
  return [a?.f(a.c), a?.arr[a.c], a?.g().f(a.c)];
}
function truthyCondition(a: O | undefined) {
  let x: number;
  if (a?.f((x = 1))) return x;
  return 0;
}
function negatedCondition(a: O | undefined) {
  let x: number;
  return !a?.f((x = 1)) || x;
}
function ternaryCondition(a: O | undefined) {
  let x: number;
  return a?.f((x = 3)) ? x : -1;
}
function coalesced(a: O | undefined) {
  let x: number;
  a?.f((x = 4)) ?? (x = 5);
  return x;
}

console.log(narrowedArgument(o), narrowedArgument(undefined));
console.log(truthyCondition(o), truthyCondition(undefined));
console.log(negatedCondition(o), negatedCondition(undefined));
console.log(ternaryCondition(o), ternaryCondition(undefined));
console.log(coalesced(o), coalesced(undefined));
